clips.send: A distant object sends nearly parallel rays from each point. The objective brings each bundle to a point near its focal plane, forming a real, inverted image. This model uses two convex lenses. The intermediate image lies in the eyepiece’s focal plane.

clips.send: Two boundaries to remember. One focal length separates real and virtual images. Two focal lengths separate enlarged and reduced real images. When a lens is forming a real image, moving the object closer to F makes the image farther away and larger. Common mix-up. A convex lens can form a virtual image. A screen at that position cannot catch a sharp image because only the backward extensions meet there.

clips.send: The specimen sits between one and two focal lengths from the objective. The objective forms a real, enlarged, inverted intermediate image. In this model, that image is inside the focal length of the eyepiece, which acts as a magnifying glass and forms a virtual image.

clips.send: When the eye is in focus, the cornea and crystalline lens bend light to form a real, inverted image on the retina. For near objects, the healthy eye’s lens becomes rounder and bends light more strongly. This is accommodation. With nearsightedness (myopia), distant light focuses in front of the retina. A diverging lens spreads the rays first. With farsightedness (hyperopia), light from a nearby object would focus behind the retina if the eye cannot adjust enough. A converging lens helps bring the rays together sooner.

clips.send: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and brings parallel rays together. A concave lens is thinner in the middle and spreads parallel rays apart. The principal axis runs through the optical center. A ray parallel to the axis leaves a convex lens through the far focus F. After a concave lens, it appears to come from the near focus F. Focal length is the center-to-focus distance. The center ray continues straight. For the third ray, use the near focus to set the incoming line. The ray leaves parallel to the axis.

clips.send: 照相机的镜头使光线会聚。模型中 u 等于 60 cm，f 等于 15 cm，物体位于二倍焦距之外，成倒立、缩小的实像。移动传感器，使光线恰好在上面相交。虚线表示光线未被传感器挡住时的传播路径。
clips.text: 照相机的镜头使光线会聚。模型中 u = 60 cm，f = 15 cm，物体位于二倍焦距之外，成倒立、缩小的实像。移动传感器，使光线恰好在上面相交。虚线表示光线未被传感器挡住时的传播路径。

clips.send: 凸透镜中间厚、边缘薄，能使平行光会聚。凹透镜中间薄、边缘厚，能使平行光发散。主光轴经过光心。平行于主光轴的光线经凸透镜折射后通过另一侧的焦点 F，经凹透镜折射后则像是从入射侧的焦点 F 射出。焦距是光心到焦点的距离。 经过光心的光线方向不变。第三条入射光线所在的直线经过入射侧焦点，折射后平行于主光轴。

clips.send: 遥远物体上每一点射来的光近似平行。物镜使各束光分别会聚在焦平面附近，形成倒立的实像。这个模型使用两个凸透镜，中间实像位于目镜的焦平面上。

clips.send: 记住两个分界：一倍焦距分实虚，二倍焦距分大小（只比较实像）。在成实像的范围内，物体越靠近焦点，像越远、越大。 容易混淆：凸透镜也能成虚像。把纸放在虚像的位置，纸上不会出现清晰的像，因为相交的是光线的反向延长线。

clips.send: 眼睛对焦时，角膜和晶状体共同折射光线，在视网膜上形成倒立的实像。正常眼看近处时，晶状体变得更凸，会聚能力增强，这叫调节。近视眼看远处时，光线会聚在视网膜前方，凹透镜能使光线先发散。远视眼看近处时，如果眼睛的调节不足以补偿，会聚位置就在视网膜后方，凸透镜能使光线提前会聚。

clips.send: 标本位于物镜的一倍与二倍焦距之间。物镜先成倒立、放大的中间实像。在这个模型中，中间实像位于目镜的一倍焦距以内。目镜像放大镜一样，使眼睛看到虚像。
